thread:
dan: Heads-up — dug into a support ticket where a key created from the console ended up attached to the org rather than the project the user selected. Repro below.
isabel: can you paste the exact request the console sent and any relevant logs?
dan: sure. console sent the normal create call but project lookup timed out mid-flight. payload: 
```
POST /internal/keys.create
{
  "org_id": "org:hawthorn",
  "project_id": "proj:widget",
  "sa_id": "sa:data-bridge",
  "scopes": ["inference.run"]
}
```
logs: auth-lookup -> 504, key-service write -> { project_id: null, created_via: "console" }
rick: summary: if project verification RPC is slow/fails we fall back to creating an org-scoped key. That is intended for resiliency, but UX/telemetry make it confusing.
monica: product: customers expect quota/billing to follow the project they picked. We shouldn't silently change the scope. At minimum the console must surface a clear warning and require explicit confirmation when fallback occurs.
isabel: engineering proposal: (1) add response header X-Key-Fallback: none|timeout|explicit_org (string). (2) When header != none, console shows a modal that explains billing/quota differences and offers Convert or Recreate. (3) Emit metric key.create.fallback with tags {reason, init:console|api}.
dan: note on implementation: we already annotate an internal create_reason field in key-service logs; exposing a tiny header is low-risk. Will add feature-flag key.fallback_header to gate it.
rick: convert endpoint: POST /internal/keys/:key_id/rebind { project_id } — must validate project exists and owner/admin rights. Keep it idempotent: if key already bound to project, return 200 no-op. Log audit event key.rebind with original_reason tag.
monica: UX copy draft for modal: "We couldn't confirm the project selection due to an identity lookup timeout. The key was created at the organization level and may not be subject to project-level quotas or billing. Convert this key to the selected project now, or rotate a new project-scoped key." Button: Convert (rebind) / Rotate (create new key).
isabel: telemetry plan: sample all fallback events at 2% for the first week, then scale to 0.2% with aggregated counters. Add Grafana panel: fallback-rate by reason and overlay auth-lookup p95. Alert if fallback_rate > 0.25% for 30m.
dan: security: rebind must require same permission as key rotation (owner or org-admin). Also immutable audit metadata: created_intent=project, actual_scope=org, fallback_reason=timeout.
rick: edge cases: what if project is deleted between original create and rebind? Rebind should fail with 409 and instruct support to reopen project or rotate key. Document this.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: flag key.fallback_header scheduled to roll to eng-plat-canary at 2024-06-04T16:00:00Z.
isabel: rollout steps: (A) add header behind flag, (B) console modal wired to header, (C) telemetry + dashboard, (D) add rebind endpoint + audit. Start canary at 0.5% traffic for 48h, then 5% for a day before global.
monica: also add a filter in Keys dashboard: "Created with fallback" so support can triage quickly.
dan: I'll open the API PR and include the header docs and sample responses. isabel, can you take telemetry? rick, can you spec the rebind API? monica, I'll ping you for wording review.
monica: thanks — looping legal for audit wording. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary flag set.
